articles.title: Vitamin D deficiency alters prostate epithelial differentiation and increases prostate cancer aggressiveness in ex vivo and in vivo models.
articles.abstract: Here, we examined the consequences of biologically relevant vitamin D deficiency, a known risk factor for aggressive prostate cancer, using ex vivo and in vivo models. Phenotypic and single-cell RNA sequencing of mouse prostate organoids showed that vitamin D deficiency stunted luminal cell differentiation more than androgen deficiency, which is a known driver of prostate development. Mice fed a vitamin D-deficient diet showed significantly altered expression of androgen-responsive genes in their prostate luminal cells, as determined by single-cell RNA sequencing. MDA-PCa-2b and 22Rv1 human prostate cancer cells, when maintained for 6 months in 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, had very different responses compared to short-term treatments. Notably, the MDA-PCa-2b cells lost the ability to form xenografts, despite normal proliferation in vitro. RNA sequencing showed that these cells also had disruptions in androgen signaling and in multiple cancer-related pathways, which differed by treatment duration. This study offers new insights and validation of vitamin D's role in both benign and malignant prostate biology, underscoring its essential hormonal functions and supporting strategies for vitamin D supplementation to reduce prostate cancer risk in vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Novel Piperlongumine derivatives exert multimodal antitumor effects in prostate cancer via MAPK pathway activation, poly-mechanistic apoptosis induction, and DNMT3A-mediated DNA methylation reduction.
articles.abstract: The high mortality rate of prostate cancer remains a major threat to men's health worldwide, highlighting an urgent need for novel therapeutic agents with improved efficacy and safety profiles. In this study, we employed a rational structural modification strategy to synthesize 14 novel 1,2,3-triazole-hybridized derivatives of piperlongumine (PL), a natural alkaloid with proven anticancer activity. The antiproliferative activity of these derivatives was evaluated in vitro against multiple cancer cell lines (PC-3, A549, T47D, and SMMC-7721), with normal HEK293 cells used to assess their selectivity. All synthesized derivatives (1 M-14 M) exhibited significant antitumor efficacy, with lead compound 11 M showing pronounced inhibition of PC-3 cell proliferation and migration. Mechanistic studies revealed that 11 M induced G2/M phase arrest and triggered mitochondrial-dependent apoptosis, while concurrently activating the ROS-MAPK signaling pathway and autophagic flux. Notably, 11 M attenuated DNMT3A-mediated global DNA hypomethylation. In vivo validation in PC-3 xenograft mice confirmed that 11 M exerted robust tumor growth suppression with low systemic toxicity, accompanied by DNMT3A downregulation and MAPK pathway activation, substantiating its multi-target therapeutic mechanism.

articles.title: Boosting Diagnostic Accuracy of Prostate Cancer: Combining Clinical PSA Level and a Pair of NIR Fluorescent Probes for SLC39A1 and PSMA.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a leading malignancy in men globally. Although serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing is prevalent for PCa screening, its inherent limitation in specificity and sensitivity frequently leads to high false-positive and false-negative diagnoses. To address this challenge, we present a PSA+ strategy that integrates a clinically defined PSA threshold (10 ng/mL) with a pair of complementary near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent probes: a zinc-complex-based probe (Cy-O-NS-a-Zn) targeting the zinc transporter solute carrier family 39 member 1 (SLC39A1), and a glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-Urea-Lys) ligand-based probe (Cy-S-Glu) targeting prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA). This combinatorial approach accurately discriminates PCa from normal prostate cells, delineates tumor margins in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) mouse models with robust tumor-to-background ratios (TBR), and enables fluorescence-guided surgery. Importantly, a double-blind histopathological validation using 70 cases of human prostate tissue specimens revealed that the PSA+ strategy substantially outperformed PSA testing alone, improving diagnostic specificity from 70% to 97.6% and sensitivity from 75% to 96.8%. Collectively, this work provides a rapid, accurate, and comprehensive diagnostic paradigm that complements standard PSA testing, thereby refining clinical diagnosis and decision-making in PCa.

articles.title: Quercetin attenuates polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastic-induced malignant phenotypes linked to APOE stabilization and lipid metabolic reprogramming in prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are emerging environmental contaminants with increasing evidence of biological activity in mammalian systems. However, the molecular mechanisms by which chronic polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastic (PET-NPs) exposure promotes prostate cancer progression, and whether this process can be attenuated by quercetin, remain poorly understood. DU-145 and LNCaP cells were subjected to repeated PET-NPs exposure and analyzed using functional assays, DIA proteomics, protein-stability and ubiquitination assays, APOE loss- and gain-of-function experiments, and xenograft models. PET-NPs enhanced proliferation, migration, invasion, intracellular lipid accumulation, and tumor growth. Proteomic analysis highlighted cholesterol metabolism, lipid transport, and PI3K/AKT signaling, leading to prioritization of APOE. PET-NPs increased APOE protein abundance without altering APOE mRNA, prolonged APOE protein stability, and reduced its ubiquitination-dependent proteasomal turnover. APOE knockdown attenuated PET-NPs-induced increases in triglyceride and total cholesterol levels, PIK3CA expression, AKT phosphorylation, proliferation, migration, and invasion, supporting APOE as an important but non-exclusive functional contributor. Quercetin reduced APOE mRNA and protein abundance and suppressed PET-NPs-associated lipid accumulation, PI3K/AKT activation, and malignant phenotypes in vitro. APOE overexpression partially restored PIK3CA expression, AKT phosphorylation, total cholesterol levels, EdU incorporation, invasion, and migration in both DU-145 and LNCaP cells under PET-NPs plus quercetin treatment, whereas the restoration of triglyceride levels reached statistical significance only in LNCaP cells. In vivo, quercetin attenuated PET-NPs-associated subcutaneous and orthotopic tumor progression and reduced APOE, p-AKT, PLIN2, Ki-67, and MMP2 staining. These findings indicate that APOE contributes to, but does not fully account for, the inhibitory effects of quercetin.

articles.title: Discovery of Biaryl amide-containing transmembrane serine protease 2 (TMPRSS2) inhibitors for the treatment of prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: Transmembrane serine protease 2 (TMPRSS2) is an important driver of prostate tumor progression and represents a promising therapeutic target for prostate cancer treatment. Guided by the lead scaffold avoralstat, we designed and synthesized a series of novel compounds to systematically explore their structure-activity relationships (SARs) against TMPRSS2. Among them, compound XDTM13 (IC<sub>50</sub> = 3.60 nM) and XDTM14 (IC<sub>50</sub> = 34.6 nM) exhibited potent TMPRSS2 inhibitory activity, with XDTM13 demonstrating markedly superior potency compared to avoralstat (IC<sub>50</sub> = 18.2 nM). Western blot analysis confirmed that XDTM13 and XDTM14 effectively suppressed TMPRSS2 autoproteolysis, while transwell assays further demonstrated their inhibition of LNCaP cell migration and invasion. Furthermore, XDTM13 and XDTM14 showed improved metabolic stability in human liver microsomes relative to avoralstat. Collectively, these results indicate that XDTM13 and XDTM14 are promising lead compounds for TMPRSS2 inhibition, with XDTM13 emerging as a particularly potent candidate for further development.

Baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D and progression-free survival in de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: prognostic model development and external validation.
articles.abstract: Prognostic biomarkers for risk stratification remain limited in de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) treated with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs). We evaluated baseline serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] and developed and externally validated a progression-free survival (PFS) model. This multicenter retrospective study included 273 patients initiating ARPI-based therapy between January 2021 and April 2026. Etlik City Hospital formed the training cohort (n = 192; 85 PFS events), and Gazi University and Kütahya City Hospital formed the external validation cohort (n = 81; 27 PFS events). LASSO-penalized Cox regression retained age, ISUP grade group, CHAARTED disease volume, log-transformed PSA, and hemoglobin. Model B added continuous 25(OH)D. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples. Performance was assessed by the Harrell C-index, time-dependent AUC, and calibration at 1 and 2 years. PFS was the primary endpoint; overall survival analyses were exploratory. The study was not prospectively registered. Higher baseline 25(OH)D was associated with longer PFS in Model B (HR per 10-ng/mL increase, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.49-0.83; P < .001). Adding 25(OH)D improved model fit (likelihood-ratio χ² = 12.71; P < .001) and increased apparent C-index from 0.712 to 0.740. In external validation, C-indices were 0.71 (95% CI, 0.64-0.78) and 0.76 (95% CI, 0.69-0.83), respectively (Δ = 0.05; 95% CI, 0.01-0.10). Baseline 25(OH)D added modest prognostic information beyond clinical factors, with supportive external validation. These findings do not establish treatment-predictive utility or benefit from vitamin D supplementation. Prospective validation is needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Non-histone protein lactylation in cancer metastasis: From metabolic reprogramming to therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: Cancer metastasis remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and tumor metabolic reprogramming, particularly aerobic glycolysis and lactate accumulation, is increasingly recognized as a metastatic driver. Lysine lactylation provides a direct mechanism by which lactate modifies proteins to shape tumor behavior. Although initially characterized on histones as an epigenetic mark, lactylation is now widely distributed on non-histone proteins, where it functions as a metabolism-linked post-translational modification (PTM) regulating metastatic dissemination. Non-histone lactylation promotes epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) through modification of EMT transcription factors and a PRMT1-vimentin axis in triple-negative breast cancer. Lactylation enhances tumor invasion and survival by stabilizing oncoproteins via ubiquitination inhibition, reprogramming metabolic flux, and activating oncogenic transcription. PD-L1 lactylation enables immune evasion, while lactylation of DNA repair proteins confers therapy resistance. Recent findings expand resistance mechanisms to include cuproptosis evasion through MTF1 lactylation in castration-resistant prostate cancer. Positive feedback loops lock tumor cells into glycolytic, lactylation-rich states reinforcing metastasis. Both lactylation and delactylation exert context-dependent oncogenic or tumor-suppressive effects, as illustrated by PARK7, functioning as a writer in hepatocellular carcinoma yet as a delactylase promoting antitumor immunity. We synthesize how non-histone lactylation regulates the metastatic cascade using a three-tier confidence framework distinguishing fully characterized circuits from proteomic screening hits, and discuss therapeutic strategies ranging direct lactylation machinery inhibitors from indirect lactate-axis modulators. Lactylation also drives organ-specific metastatic colonization and emerges as a clinical biomarker for metastasis risk stratification. These mechanisms may reveal new opportunities for lactylation-targeted therapies, though significant challenges in selectivity, toxicity, and biomarker validation remain.

articles.title: The impact of the tumor microenvironment on immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance in prostate cancer: Mechanistic insights and therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the treatment landscape for melanoma and lung cancer, their efficacy in prostate cancer (PCa) remains limited. This therapeutic resistance is linked in part to the "cold" immunophenotype of PCa, which is orchestrated by a highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Current evidence suggests that distinct spatial barriers and metabolic dysregulation within the TME actively exclude effector lymphocytes and induce exhaustion. Here, we dissect these multidimensional resistance mechanisms, ranging from myeloid cell plasticity to stromal stiffening. We further evaluate how clinical paradigms are shifting from monotherapy to rational combinations, such as those involving poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors or anti-angiogenic agents, designed to reprogram the TME. Finally, by exploring emerging frontiers including neuroendocrine transdifferentiation, nanobiotechnology, and liquid biopsy, we propose a roadmap for next-generation therapies aimed at sensitizing PCa to immune recognition.

articles.title: Wine intake and cancer risk: An umbrella review of meta-analyses.
articles.abstract: Alcohol consumption is a known risk factor for cancer, but different alcoholic beverages may be differently associated with cancer risk. Wine is a complex hydro-alcoholic solution containing several compounds with potential anti-carcinogenic properties. This umbrella review aimed to summarize the available evidence on the association between wine consumption and cancer risk across different cancer sites. A systematic search was conducted on PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science, including systematic reviews and meta-analyses published up to April 28, 2026. The methodological quality of the included meta-analyses was evaluated using AMSTAR-2. The strength of evidence was assessed considering statistical significance, number of cases, heterogeneity and small-study effects. Pooled analyses were considered separately. Twenty-seven meta-analyses were included. Most of the associations between wine consumption and cancer risk were not statistically significant. No significant associations were generally found for colorectal, gastric, bladder, endometrial, ovarian and lung cancers. An increased risk was reported for oral and pharyngeal cancer (RR 2.12, 95% CI 1.37-3.29) and esophageal cancer (RR 5.34, 95% CI 1.43-19.89). The available evidence regarding specific beverage types (red versus white wine) was highly inconsistent across the evaluated cancer sites. For breast cancer, risk estimates were remarkably similar between white and red wine, while findings for prostate cancer showed conflicting directions across the included meta-analyses, preventing definitive conclusions regarding beverage-specific effects. The available evidence showed a heterogeneous association between wine consumption and cancer risk across different cancer sites. While most associations were not statistically significant, increased risks were reported for some malignancies. However, the heterogeneity and methodological limitations of the available evidence do not allow definitive conclusions regarding the specific role of wine in cancer risk.

articles.title: Mechanism-Informed Language Modeling and Oxygenated 3D Screening Identify Berberine-Enzalutamide Synergy in Prostate Cancer Models.
articles.abstract: Combination therapies are key to overcoming resistance to androgen receptor (AR) signaling inhibitors in prostate cancer. Current paradigms for developing synergistic therapies, however, remain chronically inefficient and resource-intensive due to the prohibitive scale of the combinatorial screening space and a lack of computational frameworks for navigating signaling crosstalk. This work introduces a hybrid in silico and in vitro lead discovery platform that integrates knowledge-augmented large language models (LLMs) with an oxygen-supplemented 3D spheroid system. By comparing compound mechanism-of-action annotations with disease-relevant signaling crosstalk, the LLM framework nominates drug pairs with predictive performance and interpretable, pathway-based rationales. This computational pipeline is complemented by an engineered 3D spheroid model that utilizes oxygen supplementation to mitigate artifactual necrosis, a common confounder that masks synergistic signals in standard screening. Using this approach to screen 3,592 natural products, we identified berberine-enzalutamide as an in vitro combination hit that re-sensitized resistant prostate cancer cells to AR blockade. Molecular and transcriptomic profiling revealed changes in mTORC1 and AMPK signaling that were consistent with the pathway-based hypothesis generated by LLM. These results establish proof of concept that mechanism-informed language modeling coupled with 3D screening can prioritize and experimentally evaluate drug-combination hypotheses at an early stage of discovery.

articles.title: PRMT7 at the crossroads of cancer progression and therapeutic targeting (Review).
articles.abstract: Protein arginine methyltransferase 7 (PRMT7), the sole type III PRMT family member, catalyzes arginine monomethylation and has recently emerged as an important regulator of cancer biology. Increasing evidence indicates that PRMT7 participates in tumor initiation and progression through epigenetic regulation, transcriptional control, RNA processing and signaling pathway modulation. Dysregulated PRMT7 expression has been reported in diverse malignancies, including leukemia, breast cancer, lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, prostate cancer and gastric cancer. Functionally, PRMT7 has been implicated in epithelial‑mesenchymal transition, cancer stemness, metastasis and immune modulation, although its effects may vary depending on cellular and tumor context. The present review summarizes the structural and biochemical features of PRMT7, its mechanistic roles across different cancer types, and its potential as a therapeutic target. Recent progress in PRMT inhibitor development was also discussed, with particular emphasis on PRMT7‑selective compounds such as SGC3027, SGC8158 and JS1310, as well as the key challenges that remain for clinical translation. Elucidating the context‑specific functions and targetable vulnerabilities of PRMT7 may provide new opportunities for precision cancer therapy.

articles.title: Structural basis of serine protease inhibition by antibodies from biased Fab phage-display libraries.
articles.abstract: Biased Fab phage-display libraries were designed to determine whether inhibitory CDR H3 motifs from potent anti-matriptase antibodies could be transferred to target homologous serine proteases. Using reverse-binding and substrate-like H3 motifs from parental clones A11 and E2 as templates, six synthetic libraries with 10<sup>10</sup> diversity were constructed. Selection against matriptase identified 16 inhibitors with sub-100 nM potency, representing 100,000-fold improvement over circularized H3 loops alone. Selection against TMPRSS2, a serine protease implicated in viral entry and prostate cancer with 43 % sequence identity to matriptase, yielded binders with micromolar inhibitory potency. Selection against urokinase plasminogen activator (uPA, 35 % identity) identified binders that adopted a substrate-like CDR H3 binding mode in our structural models. Across all reference structures, including the separately identified uPA inhibitor AB2 (PDB: 9PYF, deposited with this work), benchmarking of five co-folding methods and rigid-body docking showed that co-folding consistently achieved acceptable to high quality DockQ scores, outperforming traditional docking and capturing the recognition of key active site determinants. Ensemble predictions of mutational binding energy changes (ΔΔG) using these models identified key paratope-epitope interactions, with predictions validated through mutagenesis. This work establishes a framework integrating biased antibody libraries with computational structure prediction and analysis for targeting conserved protease epitopes.

articles.title: Passenger co-deletion confounds glutaminolysis signatures anchored on PTEN loss: A cautionary case for location-aware signature design.
articles.abstract: PTEN-deficient tumors are widely assumed to be glutamine-dependent, a view that has helped motivate the clinical development of glutaminase inhibitors. Whether glutaminolytic transcription scales with PTEN copy-number loss in human tumors, and by what mechanism, has not been established. We classified TCGA PanCancer Atlas tumors by GISTIC copy number as PTEN intact, hemizygous, or homozygous deletion, and scored a five-gene glutaminolysis signature (GLS, SLC1A5, GOT1, GLUD1, GPT2) against loss severity across fourteen tumor types, testing MYC mediation and chromosome-10 co-deletion as alternative mechanisms, with GLS dependence assessed in DepMap CRISPR data. The signature decreased with PTEN loss in all fourteen types, significantly in twelve, but was not MYC-mediated. The decline tracked chromosomal position rather than pathway membership: GLUD1 and GOT1 flank PTEN on 10q, and thirty-seven neighboring genes carrying no glutaminolysis annotation tracked PTEN copy number just as closely (mean rho 0.843 compared with 0.842), with co-deletion fidelity falling monotonically with distance from PTEN (rho = -0.993). Adjustment for genome-wide aneuploidy left the association intact, whereas conditioning on each gene's own copy number abolished it for the chromosome-10 genes and left the others unchanged. In a natural experiment contrasting PTEN point-mutant, copy-neutral tumors with copy-neutral wild-type tumors, GLUD1 was lower in the mutant group when all cohorts were pooled (P = 1.0 x 10^-8), an effect attributable to endometrial carcinoma, the one lineage in which mutation alone lowered GLUD1; excluding that lineage in a post hoc sensitivity analysis left no detectable difference (P = 0.22, equivalence P = 0.015), whereas hemizygous and homozygous deletion lowered GLUD1 dose-dependently in every analysis. GLS dependence did not differ across dosage tiers. Prostate carcinoma was the sole departure in the negative direction, its off-chromosome-10 decline surviving adjustment for tumor purity, stage, ERG status and proliferation, opposite in direction to the signaling prediction; breast and stomach showed small positive associations. The inverse PTEN-glutaminolysis relationship in this transcript signature is therefore explained predominantly by passenger co-deletion rather than by a PTEN-linked metabolic program, making PTEN copy number unreliable as a stand-alone glutaminolysis biomarker and illustrating a general hazard: any signature scored against a frequently co-deleted locus can be confounded by where its genes sit. We provide a four-step screening procedure: decompose the signature by chromosomal position relative to the driver; test each constituent gene's own copy number against the driver's; compare driver-mutant copy-neutral tumors with copy-neutral wild-type tumors; and check the inferred pathway activity against an independent functional readout.

articles.title: USP11 Drives Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Via Promoting Ferroptosis by Deubiquitinating and Stabilizing ASK1.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) represents a pivotal pathological mechanism underlying ischemic cerebrovascular disorders including cerebral stroke. Currently, there are lack of effective preventive or therapeutic methods. Ubiquitin-specific protease 11 (USP11) is a member of the most prevalent ubiquitination-specific protease (USP) family. It has been shown that USP11 plays diverse and significant roles in a variety of diseases, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, prostate cancer, and intervertebral disc degeneration. However, its precise function and molecular mechanisms involvement in CIRI remain unknown. USP11 knockout (USP11-KO) and adeno-associated virus 9-mediated USP11 over-expression (USP11-OE) mice were established as a mouse model of CIRI, and USP11 knockdown and overexpression adenovirus were used to establish a cell model, to investigate the effect of USP11 on CIRI in vivo and in vitro. Molecular biological studies were used to clarify the mechanism of USP11 mediated ferroptosis during CIRI. The expression of USP11 is increased during CIRI. Functionally, USP11 deficiency attenuated neurological deficits, cerebral infarction, neuroinflammation, and ferroptosis during CIRI, whereas specific overexpression of USP11 exacerbated these pathological processes. Furthermore, USP11 knockdown inhibited neuronal injury, inflammatory response and ferroptosis, while USP11 overexpression promoted these processes. Mechanistically, USP11 bind to ASK1 and inhibit its K48-linked ubiquitination, thereby enhancing the activity of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling pathway. More importantly, the regulation of USP11 on neuronal ferroptosis and CIRI relied on its regulation of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling axis. Our study clarified the new functions and mechanisms of USP11 during CIRI. Targeting USP11-ASK1-JNK/p38-ferroptosis may be a new promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of CIRI.

articles.title: Androgen receptor-regulated ZNF419 modulates ferroptosis sensitivity via the ZDHHC20-GPX4 pathway in prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has recently been recognized as a crucial determinant of therapeutic response in prostate cancer (PCa). However, how androgen receptor (AR) signaling regulates ferroptotic susceptibility remains poorly understood. Here, we identify ZNF419, a previously uncharacterized zinc finger protein, as an AR-regulated factor associated with reduced ferroptosis susceptibility in PCa cells. Transcriptomic profiling and functional validation revealed that ZNF419 expression is markedly elevated in PCa and correlates with poor clinical outcome. Promoter-proximal AR occupancy was detected at predicted ARE-containing regions of the ZNF419 locus and contributed to ZNF419 promoter activation in reporter assays, whereas enzalutamide treatment or AR knockdown reduced ZNF419 expression and increased ferroptosis-associated vulnerability. Mechanistically, ZNF419 promotes ZDHHC20 expression and is associated with activation of a candidate downstream enhancer region. ZDHHC20, a palmitoyltransferase, contributes to GPX4 palmitoylation-associated stabilization and limits ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation of GPX4. Pharmacological interference with palmitoylation attenuates ZNF419-associated GPX4 stabilization, whereas ZDHHC20 restoration partially reverses the increased ferroptosis-associated vulnerability of ZNF419-deficient cells. Collectively, our findings support a previously unrecognized AR-associated ZNF419-ZDHHC20-GPX4 regulatory axis that links AR activity to ferroptosis-associated vulnerability. These findings provide a rationale for further investigating whether modulation of this pathway may influence responses to AR-targeted therapy in advanced PCa.

articles.title: Multiple-Session Magnetic Fluid Hyperthermia: Augmented MNPs Penetration Led to Complete Eradication of Hetero-Multicellular Breast Tumor Spheroids via Apoptosis.
articles.abstract: Magnetic fluid hyperthermia (MFH) is an emerging localized cancer therapy that uses magnetic nanoparticles to selectively induce 42 to 45 °C mild hyperthermia within tumor tissues under alternating magnetic field to kill cancer cells. Despite encouraging clinical outcomes in glioblastoma and prostate cancer, the broader clinical translation of MFH across various tumor types remains limited by heterogeneous nanoparticle distribution, inconsistent tumor heating, and the frequent use of poorly predictive preclinical two-dimensional (2D) cultures. These conventional cultures fail to recapitulate the structural and stromal complexity of solid tumors and often overestimate therapeutic efficacy. In an attempt to recreate the cellular heterogeneity of clinical breast tumors to some extent, we developed a hetero-multicellular spheroid of breast cancer by co-culturing breast adenocarcinoma cells MCF-7, with non-cancerous murine fibroblasts McCoy. This approach generated heterospheroids that mimic certain key features of the breast tumor microenvironment, including heterogeneous cell population, fibroblast activation, collagen-rich extracellular matrix deposition, and the spatial arrangement of proliferative, quiescent, and necrotic cells. Following histologic validation, the hyperthermic potential of poly(acrylic acid)-coated Mn0.9Zn0.1Fe2O4 nanoparticle-based magnetic fluid on the heterospheroids was assessed under a 10 kA/m magnetic field strength and 332 kHz frequency. A single-session MFH inhibited heterospheroid growth and induced apoptosis; however, it did not significantly ablate the spheroids. Subsequently, two MFH sessions led to the complete elimination of the spheroids, accompanied by pronounced apoptotic activity. These findings suggest that repeated MFH can overcome thermotolerance, thereby augmenting therapeutic potential against stromal-rich breast tumors.

articles.title: Real-World HRR Testing Pathways and Patterns of Detected Alterations in Prostate Cancer From the Multinational ARON-3 Study.
articles.abstract: Homologous recombination repair (HRR) testing is increasingly relevant in prostate cancer because it identifies patients who may benefit from biomarker-guided treatment strategies, including poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi). However, real-world implementation of HRR testing remains variable across countries and clinical settings, and the extent to which current testing pathways capture actionable alterations is not well defined. ARON-3 is a multinational, multicentre, retrospective real-world study of patients with prostate cancer. In this subanalysis, we assessed genomic testing uptake within the overall ARON-3 cohort and characterised HRR testing pathways and detected pathogenic alterations among patients with available genomic results. Genomic testing included germline, somatic tumour, and/or circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) assays performed in routine practice across participating centres. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify clinicopathologic factors associated with undergoing genomic HRR testing. Among 2,192 patients included in ARON-3, genomic testing results were available for 719 (33%). Among tested patients, 660 (92%) underwent germline testing and 610 (85%) somatic testing; 549 (77%) underwent both, whereas 109 (15%) had germline-only and 61 (8%) somatic-only testing. In multivariable analysis, metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, high-volume disease, and Gleason score > 8 were independently associated with higher odds of testing, while age ≥ 70 years was associated with lower odds of testing. Overall, 238 tested patients (33%) harboured pathogenic HRR alterations, corresponding to 11% of the entire ARON-3 cohort. Somatic pathogenic alterations were more frequent than germline alterations. BRCA2 was the most frequently altered gene, while non-BRCA1/2 alterations were also detected, particularly in centres using broader multigene panels. Most centres relied on BRCA1/2-focused assays, and the use of liquid biopsy remained limited. This multinational real-world analysis demonstrates substantial heterogeneity in HRR testing uptake and testing pathways across participating ARON-3 centres. Testing was more commonly performed in patients with more advanced disease features, suggesting that clinically relevant subgroups may still be differentially selected for genomic assessment. Broader and more standardised implementation of comprehensive HRR profiling may improve the identification of actionable alterations and strengthen precision medicine in prostate cancer.

articles.title: Fracture risk and fracture risk factor assessment among men at prostate cancer diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Older men with prostate cancer, particularly those receiving androgen deprivation therapy, have an increased fracture risk. However, contemporary studies assessing baseline fracture risk in ethnically diverse populations of men at initial prostate cancer diagnosis remain limited. Men aged 50-89 years with newly diagnosed prostate cancer (2010-2022) in a US integrated healthcare system were identified. Demographic data, smoking, prior fracture, rheumatoid arthritis, recent glucocorticoid therapy, body mass index (FRAX variables), and other risk factors (diabetes, low 25OH-vitamin D level) were ascertained from electronic health records. Ten-year risks of hip (10yHIP) and major osteoporotic fractures (10yMOF) were calculated using the US FRAX (race/ethnicity-specific, without bone density); additional scores removed race/ethnicity calibration. High fracture risk was defined as 10yMOF ≥ 20% and 10yHIP ≥ 3%. Among 25,413 men with prostate cancer (mean age 66.1 ± 8.1 years; 64.8% White, 12.3% Black, 10.7% Hispanic, 11.5% Asian/Pacific Islander (PI)), 87.5%, 3.4%, and 9.1% had local or locally advanced disease, node-positive, and metastatic disease, respectively. Overall, 7.2% smoked, 20.4% had diabetes, and 6.4% had a prior fracture with demographic variation; <1% had rheumatoid arthritis or extended glucocorticoid therapy. Few (0.2%) had 10yMOF ≥ 20% but 11.6% had 10yHIP ≥ 3%, ranging from 15.5% (White), 7.3% (Asian/PI), 4.8% (Hispanic) and 1.4% (Black) and increasing to 14.9% (Asian/PI), 10.9% (Hispanic), and 8.1% (Black) without race/ethnicity calibration. Age was a major risk factor; 20.5% of men aged ≥65 years, increasing to 87.3% of men aged 80-89 years had 10yHIP ≥ 3%. Diabetes and hypovitaminosis D were especially prevalent among non-White populations. 1 in 9 men with prostate cancer had a high calculated hip fracture risk at diagnosis, increasing to 1 in 5 men aged ≥65 years, with key demographic differences. These observations in real-world populations underscore the importance of skeletal health assessment among older men with prostate cancer and evaluation of fracture risk assessment tools to inform clinical management.

articles.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide in high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer: a randomized phase 2 trial.
articles.abstract: Combining inhibition of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase and androgen receptor (AR) pathway has demonstrated clinical activity in men with metastatic prostate cancer, although the extent of benefit in tumors lacking homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations remains uncertain. We conducted a randomized phase 2 trial evaluating talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in men with high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer (mHNPC). Fifty-four patients starting androgen deprivation therapy received two cycles of enzalutamide lead-in before 1:2 randomization to enzalutamide (n = 17) or enzalutamide plus talazoparib (n = 37). The primary endpoint was met, with a 73% prostate-specific antigen (PSA) <0.2 ng ml<sup>-1</sup> response rate at 12 months in the combination arm (95% confidence interval (CI) = 56-86%), exceeding the prespecified efficacy threshold (P < 0.001); the PSA <0.2 rate in the control arm was 64.7% (95% CI = 38-86%, P = 0.54 for exploratory comparison between arms). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 68% patients receiving the combination versus 35% with enzalutamide alone, predominantly anemia (41%). Two fatal therapy-emergent myeloid neoplasms occurred in the enzalutamide plus talazoparib arm in patients with underlying genomic susceptibility. Analyses of paired tumor biopsies acquired at baseline and during enzalutamide lead-in phase demonstrated marked tumor transcriptional reprogramming after AR inhibition, including suppression of proliferation-associated and HRR-related gene expression programs, but without functional impairment of homologous recombination activity. Overall, talazoparib plus enzalutamide demonstrated clinical activity in patients with high-volume mHNPC but did not establish clear additional clinical benefit over enzalutamide alone in this biomarker-unselected population, while being associated with increased toxicity. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04332744 .

articles.title: Luteolin inhibits prostate cancer stem cells through disrupting the lactate/H3K18la/β-catenin/LDHA feedback loop.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer is one of the most common malignant tumors in men, with prostate cancer stem cells (PCSCs) playing an important role in its initiation and progression. Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that lactate and lactate-mediated histone lactylation are crucial regulators of proliferation, metastasis, immune escape and drug resistance in various cancer. However, their functional roles and underlying mechanisms in PCSCs remain largely elusive. In the present study, we found that lactate levels were significantly elevated in PCSC microenvironment, which effectively induced H3K18 lactylation (H3K18la). The increased-lactate enhanced the stemness of PCSCs. ChIP analysis revealed that H3K18la positively regulated the transcription of the β-catenin gene. Furthermore, β-catenin transcriptionally activated lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) to promote lactate production, thereby forming a lactate/H3K18la/β-catenin/LDHA positive feedback loop. Notably, luteolin, a natural flavone, disrupted this feedback loop and exerted potent inhibitory effects on PCSCs. Collectively, our findings uncover a novel lactate-driven regulatory axis in PCSCs and provide new insights into the development of intervention strategies in prostate cancer.

articles.title: Knowledge-guided identification of miR-7-5p/ACTC1 as a ferroptosis regulatory axis mediating intracellular ferrous iron accumulation in prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a common malignancy with an increasing incidence in men worldwide. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of programmed cell death mediated by interactions among multiple genes, has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for PCa. Previous work focused on modeling the contribution of literature-reported known ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs) in cancers, in this study a knowledge-guided bioinformatics model was applied by systematically characterizing the topology-function properties in PCa-specific protein-protein interaction network with known FRGs as the prior knowledge to guide the identification of novel ferroptosis-related signatures. The model starts at a random walk with restart algorithm to extract genes with global topological proximity to FRG seeds, and an integrated prioritization strategy, i.e., node centrality scoring, community module mining, and clinical significance evaluation, was proposed to identify ACTC1 as a top-prioritized candidate triggering PCa ferroptosis. The expression of ACTC1 was significantly negatively correlated with PCa pathological malignancy and biochemical recurrence (p < 0.05). Experimental validations using western blotting, intracellular reactive oxygen species, Fe<sup>2+</sup> probe FerroOrange, transmission electron microscopy, and molecular pathway detection, etc., demonstrated that ACTC1 was a biomarker and tumor suppressor with the mechanism of inhibiting PCa development via inducing abnormal intracellular Fe<sup>2+</sup> accumulation and ferroptosis. In particular, the over-expression of ACTC1 contributed to changes in Fe<sup>2+</sup> homeostasis-associated proteins, i.e., upregulating DMT1/NCOA4 (p < 0.001) and downregulating FPN1 (p < 0.01). Moreover, miR-7-5p was a potential upstream regulator of ACTC1, and it mediated the level of intracellular Fe<sup>2+</sup> and reactive oxygen species in PCa ferroptosis (p < 0.001). This study proposed an interpretable pipeline for the screening of ferroptosis-related factors, which holds the applicability to biomarker discovery in other disease scenarios.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic health's influence on the efficacy of pre-operative hormone therapy for men with localized high-risk prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: Altered lipid metabolism, adiposity, and androgens have been linked to cardiac disease and prostate cancer. Adiposity increases risk of recurrence for prostate cancer and may enhance response to androgen receptor pathway inhibition (ARPI). We evaluated whether adiposity and circulating lipid metabolites are associated with response to pre-operative ADT + /- ARPI in localized high-risk prostate cancer (HRPCa). We performed a post hoc analysis of 104 men with localized HRPCa treated with 3-6 months of preoperative ADT + /- ARPI across three trials. Body composition was quantified from L3 CT imaging at baseline and at radical prostatectomy (RP; end-of-treatment [EOT] n = 56). Plasma lipid metabolites were profiled by UPLC-MS at baseline (n = 60) and in paired baseline/EOT samples (n = 59). Pathologic response was defined as ≤ T2N0 at RP. PSA progression-free survival (PFS) was defined as time from RP to PSA ≥ 0.2 ng/mL or initiation of radiotherapy. Median age was 63 years, 76.9% had Gleason grade group 4-5, and 43.7% had clinical T3-4 disease. At RP, lower visceral (VATi, p = 0.002) and subcutaneous adiposity (SATi, p = 0.004) were associated with pathologic response. Increasing adiposity at RP was associated with PSA progression (per 10-unit increase: VATi HR 1.09, p = 0.04; SATi HR 1.14, p = 0.03). In paired analyses (n = 59), pathologic responders demonstrated decreases (p < 0.05) in diacylglycerols and polyunsaturated fatty acyl chain-containing triacylglycerols (PUFA-TAGs) and elevations in ceramide species. Non-responders exhibited increases (p < 0.05) in PUFA-TAGs and glycerophospholipids with reductions in lysophosphatidylcholine species, long-chain acylcarnitine, and cholesterol. Higher post-treatment adiposity and intrapatient changes in lipid metabolite pathways were associated with inferior outcomes after pre-operative hormone therapy, supporting a stage-dependent link between cardiometabolic health and prostate cancer that warrants further elucidation.

articles.title: Selective Cytotoxic Activity of Derivatives of the Natural Alkaloid Tetrandrine Against Cancer Cell Lines: In Vitro and In Silico Studies.
articles.abstract: Tetrandrine (TET) is a bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloid with promising anticancer activity, although its limited selectivity toward malignant over non-cancerous cells restricts its therapeutic potential. A series of mono- and bis-N-substituted tetrandrine derivatives was therefore investigated to determine whether N-functionalization could improve the cytotoxic selectivity of the parent scaffold. The series included the two new compounds MU1NT and DPBT. Following initial screening in non-cancerous ARPE-19 retinal epithelial cells, selected derivatives were evaluated against 22Rv1 prostate carcinoma, A549 lung adenocarcinoma, MDA-MB-231 triple-negative breast cancer, HCT-116 colorectal carcinoma, and HeLa cervical cancer cells. TET exhibited broad but poorly selective cytotoxicity, with IC50 values of 6.81 ± 1.79 and 6.00 ± 1.96 μM in ARPE-19 and 22Rv1 cells, respectively, corresponding to a selectivity index (SI) of 1.13. By contrast, DBT showed IC50 values of 45.44 ± 1.37 μM in ARPE-19 cells and 9.89 ± 1.08 μM in 22Rv1 cells, with an SI of 4.59, the highest experimentally determined value among the tetrandrine-based compounds evaluated. MU1NT also displayed improved selectivity toward 22Rv1 cells (SI = 2.57), although with lower cytotoxic potency than DBT. Fluorescence microscopy using DAPI and phalloidin revealed pronounced nuclear and cytoskeletal alterations in DBT-treated 22Rv1 cells, whereas ARPE-19 morphology was comparatively preserved. Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry further demonstrated an apoptosis-associated response in 22Rv1 cells, with total apoptosis reaching 86.30 ± 1.27% for TET and 34.77 ± 5.13% for DBT after 24 h at their respective MTT-derived IC50 concentrations. Molecular docking suggested distinct predicted interaction profiles for TET and DBT across the apoptosis-related proteins evaluated. Targeted redocking of co-crystallized venetoclax validated the Bcl-2 site-specific protocol (RMSD = 0.55 Å); however, both alkaloids scored less favorably than venetoclax, and the small score difference between TET and DBT did not account for their distinct cellular selectivity profiles. Collectively, these findings identify DBT as a promising tetrandrine derivative with improved selectivity, warranting further mechanistic studies and in vivo evaluation in prostate cancer models.

articles.title: Bone Quality Heterogeneity in Mixed Femoral Metastases Revealed by Stimulated Raman Scattering Spectromicroscopy.
articles.abstract: Skeletal metastases disrupt bone remodeling and compromise bone quality; however, existing analytical approaches have not provided spatially resolved characterization of chemical heterogeneity between regions of direct tumor involvement and areas distant to the tumor. Stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) spectromicroscopy is a label-free imaging technique that enables quantitative, spatially resolved assessment of tissue composition. This study characterized the organic and mineral phases of osteoblastic bone present in mixed femoral metastases using SRS microscopy, revealing whether tumor and bone interactions influence regions within the bone distant from the metastasis. Mixed metastases were induced in 5- to 6-week-old athymic male rats with ACE-1 canine prostate cancer cells via intracardiac injection. At 21-day post-inoculation, bilateral femora were harvested. Sagittal sections of the right femora were processed for histological analysis and SRS imaging of the organic phase, and undecalcified sections were used to assess the mineral phase. Regions of interest were selected within newly formed osteoblastic bone, bone distant from the tumor, and in distinct samples containing only healthy bone. Osteoblastic regions showed increases in amide I, amide III, and proline signal intensity, and a reduction in phosphate and phenylalanine signal intensities, reflecting enhanced collagen deposition with diminished mineral content and altered protein composition. Bone distant from the tumor displayed elevated proline and reduced phenylalanine signal intensity, supporting the hypothesis that tumor and bone interactions influence bone beyond areas of direct tumor involvement. These findings establish SRS microscopy as a non-destructive tool for detecting spatially resolved biochemical alterations in metastatic bone.

articles.title: PABPC1 dictates castration sensitivity in prostate cancer via orchestrating ferroptosis resistance and CD8(+) T-cell dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Resistance to next-generation androgen receptor antagonists represents a major clinical challenge in prostate cancer (PCa), underscoring the need to define its underlying mechanisms. Here, through an integrated analysis of multiple cohorts, we identify PABPC1 as an RNA-binding protein upregulated in therapy-resistant tumors, whose expression correlates with adverse clinicopathological features. Elevated PABPC1 confers enzalutamide (Enz) resistance by suppressing tumor-cell ferroptosis and CD8<sup>+</sup> T-cell cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, PABPC1 promotes the cytoplasmic colocalization of EIF4A1 with ATF4 mRNA and enhances EIF4A1-associated translation of ATF4 mRNA. Subsequently, ATF4 binds the BCAT1 promoter and transcriptionally upregulates BCAT1, thereby promoting branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) metabolic remodeling and ferroptosis resistance, with leucine emerging as a major functional contributor to both ferroptosis regulation and CD8<sup>+</sup> T-cell effector responses. In preclinical models, ixazomib restores ferroptotic vulnerability, reinvigorates T-cell activity, and synergizes with Enz, without overt histopathological abnormalities in major organs. These results identify the PABPC1-ATF4-BCAT1 axis as a key regulatory pathway linking RNA regulation with metabolic and immune reprogramming to facilitate treatment resistance in PCa.

articles.title: Obesity-Induced PLPE-PTK6-FASN Feedback Loop Drives Enzalutamide Resistance by Exacerbating Lipid Metabolic Dysregulation in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: Obesity represents an independent risk factor for various malignancies, including prostate cancer. However, how specific lipid metabolites influence enzalutamide sensitivity in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) remains elusive. Here, we find that obesity is associated with poorer clinical outcomes during enzalutamide treatment. Lipidomic profiling reveals that 1-palmitoyl-2-linoleoyl phosphatidylethanolamine (PLPE) is markedly enriched in tumors from these individuals. Mechanistically, elevated PLPE directly binds to the SH2 domain of protein tyrosine kinase 6 (PTK6), driving its membrane translocation and functional activation. Furthermore, PLPE facilitates PTK6-fatty acid synthase (FASN) interaction, enabling PTK6 to mediate FASN phosphorylation at T976 via dual mechanisms: steric occupancy and kinase cascade amplification. This hyperactivation of FASN exacerbates lipid metabolic dysregulation, ultimately conferring enzalutamide resistance. Importantly, FASN-derived palmitic acid serves as a substrate for further PLPE synthesis, thereby reinforcing PTK6 membrane retention in a positive feedback loop. Collectively, this study identifies a PLPE-PTK6-FASN feedback loop that drives lipid metabolic reprogramming and enzalutamide resistance in CRPC with obesity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of cotargeting lipid metabolism and kinase signaling.

articles.title: A Graphene Oxide-Doped CuMOF Nanoplatform Enhances Chemodynamic Therapy and Suppresses CYP2J2-Mediated Linoleic Acid Metabolism in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) responds poorly to current therapies. A tumor microenvironment-responsive nanoplatform was developed to couple chemodynamic therapy with modulation of oncogenic lipid metabolism. A graphene oxide-doped copper-based metal-organic framework (GO-CuMOF) was prepared by ultrasonicating solvothermally synthesized CuMOF with graphene oxide, and was characterized physicochemically. Its generation of hydroxyl radicals (•OH) was confirmed by a methylene blue degradation assay. Antitumor activity was evaluated in DU145 and PC3 cells and in a PC3 xenograft model. Untargeted metabolomic and proteomic profiling was integrated with data from The Cancer Genome Atlas prostate adenocarcinoma cohort, and the candidate targets were validated by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), reverse transcription quantitative PCR, and Western blotting. In the presence of glutathione (GSH), GO-CuMOF released Cu⁺, depleting GSH and generating •OH. It raised intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), induced apoptosis, and suppressed CRPC cell proliferation and xenograft growth without reducing body weight or causing overt organ toxicity. Multi-omics profiling showed CYP2J2 downregulation, with accumulation of its substrate linoleate and reduction of 9(10)- and 12(13)-epoxyoctadecenoic acid (EpOME), the latter confirmed by ELISA. CYP2J2 was the most consistently associated candidate across proteomic and public-cohort evidence. GO-CuMOF exerts concurrent chemodynamic ROS generation and CYP2J2-associated changes in linoleic acid metabolism. The CYP2J2-EpOME axis represents a candidate metabolism-directed vulnerability for CRPC that warrants functional and clinical validation.

articles.title: Spatial modulation enhances the effects of radiation on prostate cancer cells: a targeted mass spectrometry metabolomics study.
articles.abstract: Spatially modulated radiation fields, such as microbeam or grid therapy, have been shown to enhance tumor cell killing while sparing normal tissue compared to uniform fields of the same total dose. The biological mechanisms underlying this effect remain poorly understood. This study investigates metabolomic changes in prostate cancer and normal prostate cells following exposure to spatially modulated versus uniform irradiation. Prostate cancer (LNCaP) and normal prostate (PNT1A) cells were irradiated using spatially modulated or uniform fields at equivalent, higher, or lower mean doses. Metabolites from cellular extracts were profiled using targeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) selected reaction monitoring (SRM). Multivariate analyses, including principal component analysis (PCA) with bootstrapping, were applied to identify dose- and field-dependent metabolic signatures. PCA revealed a clear dose-response in uniformly irradiated LNCaP cells and distinct separation between non-irradiated and irradiated groups. Notably, cancer cells exposed to modulated fields clustered closer to those treated with a higher-dose uniform field than to those receiving the same mean dose, suggesting biological equivalence to dose escalation. Key metabolites driving this separation were associated with phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan biosynthesis pathways, indicating heightened metabolic stress under modulated irradiation. In contrast, PNT1A cells showed no significant metabolic distinction between modulated and uniform fields of the same mean dose. Spatially modulated irradiation induces metabolic responses in prostate cancer cells comparable to those elicited by higher-dose uniform fields, while normal cells respond similarly to uniform fields of the same dose. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the therapeutic advantage of spatial modulation and support its potential role in improving tumor control without increasing normal tissue toxicity. Given that clinical radiotherapy sessions typically span 15-30 minutes, incorporating spatial modulation and temporal fractionation strategies into treatment workflows may offer a practical and effective means to improve therapeutic outcomes in prostate cancer.

articles.title: Deubiquitination of WBP11 governs OPLAH-mediated glutathione biosynthesis to suppress triple programmed cell death in prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer (PC) is one of the most common male cancers. Cancer cells are well known for their capacity to avoid programed cell death (PCD) via a variety of molecular pathways, allowing them to survive oncogenic stress and therapeutic challenges. Although oncogenic splicing factors are frequently dysregulated in tumors, their functional interplay with PCD regulatory networks in PC remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we demonstrate that WBP11 exerts a pro-tumorigenic effect by promoting PC cell proliferation, while its genetic silencing triggers concurrent induction of apoptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis. Mechanistically, WBP11 directly binds to and stabilizes OPLAH mRNA, leading to elevated intracellular glutathione levels that facilitate efficient clearance of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Additionally, we demonstrate that USP13 deubiquitinates WBP11 by specifically eliminating K48-linked ubiquitin chains at lysine 626, which increases the stability of the WBP11 protein and prevents proteasomal destruction. Using a combination of in vitro functional assays, in vivo tumor models, and systematic rescue experiments, we define a previously unrecognized signaling axis, USP13-WBP11-OPLAH, that orchestrates glutathione metabolism and confers resistance to PCD, ultimately driving malignant progression of PC. Consistent with these functional findings, clinical validation reveals that USP13, WBP11, and OPLAH are significantly upregulated at the protein level in human PC tissues, and that USP13 expression positively correlates with both WBP11 and OPLAH protein abundance. Collectively, our study identifies the USP13-WBP11-OPLAH axis as a critical regulatory module linking glutathione metabolism to PCD resistance, offering promising therapeutic targets for the treatment of advanced PC.

articles.title: TRPM4 promotes ErSO-mediated oncosis-like cell death in prostate cancer cells.
articles.abstract: Advanced and treatment-refractory prostate cancer remains a major clinical challenge and requires new therapeutic strategies. The calcium-activated monovalent cation channel TRPM4 regulates cell volume and has been implicated in cancer progression. TRPM4 was recently identified as a determinant of sensitivity to Acetalax (oxyphenisatin acetate) in triple-negative breast cancer and prostate cancer; however, whether TRPM4 also determines sensitivity to ErSO in prostate cancer cells had not been tested. Here, we investigate the relationship between ErSO, which induces TRPM4-associated cytotoxicity and ERα-positive breast cancer cell death, and TRPM4 expression in prostate cancer models. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) shows a broad range of TRPM4 expression in prostate cancers, and an integrated analysis of drug-response datasets reveals a positive association between TRPM4 expression and ErSO sensitivity in prostate cancer. Functional studies demonstrate that ErSO induces rapid cellular swelling, nuclear enlargement, and membrane blebbing selectively in TRPM4-high prostate cancer cells, consistent with early oncosis-like morphological responses, whereas TRPM4-low cells are less sensitive. Time-course analyses show a downregulation of TRPM4 following ErSO treatment. Chronic ErSO exposure results in the acquisition of resistance accompanied by loss of TRPM4 expression, and ErSO-resistant cells fail to undergo ErSO-induced morphological changes. Flow cytometry analyses further show that ErSO induces loss of membrane integrity and oncosis-like cell death-associated features in TRPM4-expressing cells. These findings establish TRPM4 as a functional determinant of ErSO responsiveness in prostate cancer cells and support its potential utility as a biomarker of ErSO sensitivity.

articles.title: Prostate tissue microbiota dysbiosis associated with prostate cancer: results from the MICROPROSTK multicenter study.
articles.abstract: •The prostate harbors a diverse and previously undercharacterized microbial ecosystem with species-level resolution.•Prostate cancer (PCa) patients exhibit higher microbial richness and α-diversity in prostate tissue than non PCa patients.•Distinct microbial communities are observed across prostate, urinary, and rectal niches, independent of cancer status.•Cutibacterium acnes is enriched in PCa patients' biopsies, Lactobacillus reuteri in non-PCa patients' biopsies.•Findings highlight potential prostate-associated pathobionts and protective commensalssignatures.

articles.title: Whole-body MRI with DWIBS and choline PET/CT for detecting oligoprogressive castration-resistant prostate cancer recurrence.
articles.abstract: The diagnostic options for patients with advanced prostate cancer have expanded with the development of next-generation imaging modalities. These include whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WB-MRI) with diffusion-weighted whole-body imaging with background body signal suppression (DWIBS) and molecular positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) using choline or prostate-specific membrane antigen radiotracers. Such modalities improve the detection of whole-body nodal and bony metastases in patients with advanced prostate cancer. A 63-year-old man with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) underwent stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) targeting two pelvic nodal metastases identified by WB-MRI with DWIBS and subsequently confirmed by <sup>11</sup>C-choline PET/CT. This case highlights the potential role of <sup>11</sup>C-choline PET/CT and corresponding local treatment in the management of oligoprogressive CRPC.

articles.title: Skeletal muscle is a critical site of disrupted lipid metabolism in male hypogonadism: an in vivo interventional study.
articles.abstract: Male hypogonadism is associated with adverse cardiometabolic outcomes, however tissue-specific metabolic mechanisms underlying this phenotype remain poorly characterised. Metabolomic profiling in hypogonadism to date has been confined to plasma, with limited insights into skeletal muscle. To characterise the impact of testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) and androgen deprivation (ADT) on the plasma and skeletal muscle metabolome. Parallel prospective interventional studies examined men initiating TRT for organic hypogonadism (n=15) and ADT for prostate cancer (n=15). Participants underwent metabolic phenotyping, plasma sampling and vastus lateralis muscle biopsies pre and post intervention (6 months TRT; 3 months ADT), with untargeted metabolomic profiling of both tissues at each timepoint. TRT significantly increased serum testosterone (p<0.001) and muscle mass (p<0.05); ADT significantly reduced serum testosterone (p<0.001) and muscle mass (p<0.05) while simultaneously increasing fat mass (p<0.05). TRT significantly altered a total of 118 plasma metabolites, reflecting predominant suppression of circulating lipid species, whereas ADT altered only two. In skeletal muscle, TRT perturbed 89 metabolites and was characterised by expansion of intramuscular lipid species, while ADT altered 109 metabolites, with predominant depletion of intramuscular lipid classes. Following TRT, eight lipid classes showed divergent responses between plasma and skeletal muscle. In skeletal muscle, nine lipid classes responded differentially to TRT and ADT, including fatty acids, triacylglycerides and ceramides. This study provides the first untargeted metabolomic characterisation of skeletal muscle in response to androgen manipulation in humans. Distinct plasma and skeletal muscle responses demonstrate tissue-specific regulation that is incompletely captured by plasma profiling alone. These findings highlight skeletal muscle as a key site of androgen-sensitive metabolic regulation, providing evidence for tissue-specific lipid partitioning that may contribute to the cardiometabolic consequences of hypogonadism.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

articles.title: Monthly high-dose cholecalciferol supplementation in prostate cancer patients (ProsD trial): A nested analysis of vitamin D metabolites, metabolic ratios, and biochemical safety.
articles.abstract: The effects of intermittent, high-dose cholecalciferol supplementation on circulating vitamin D metabolites and related biomarkers remain unclear. The ProsD randomised controlled trial evaluated the effects of monthly oral supplementation with 50,000 IU cholecalciferol in males with prostate cancer and assessed longitudinal changes in vitamin D metabolite responses. To characterise vitamin D metabolites and ratios after a monthly dose of 50,000 IU cholecalciferol supplementation and to assess the effects on biochemical markers. ProsD recruited and randomised 123 men with prostate cancer; 118 participants (placebo n = 40; vitamin D n = 78) provided blood samples at baseline, and from remaining participants at 0, 6, 12, and 24 months, at follow-up visits. Plasma vitamin D metabolites-25(OH)D<sub>3</sub>, 1,25(OH)<sub>2</sub>D<sub>3</sub>, 24,25(OH)<sub>2</sub>D<sub>3</sub>, and 3-epi-25(OH)D<sub>3</sub>-and vitamin D metabolite ratios (VMRs) were quantified. Longitudinal changes and between-group differences were evaluated using age-adjusted generalised estimating equations with estimated marginal means. Routine biochemical markers were also assessed. Compared with placebo, monthly cholecalciferol supplementation increased peak between-group difference at 24 months for 25(OH)D<sub>3</sub> (+30.10 nmol/L; p < 0.01), 1,25(OH)<sub>2</sub>D<sub>3</sub> (+12.44 pmol/L; p = 0.11), 24,25(OH)<sub>2</sub>D<sub>3</sub> (+3.95 nmol/L; p < 0.01), and 3-epi-25(OH)D<sub>3</sub> (+5.94 nmol/L; p < 0.01). The 25(OH)D<sub>3</sub>:24,25(OH)<sub>2</sub>D<sub>3</sub> VMR increased in the placebo group but remained constant in the intervention group, and between-group analysis showed consistently lower ratios in the vitamin D group. All routine biomarkers remained within normal ranges throughout follow-up. Monthly oral supplementation of 50,000 IU cholecalciferol in men with prostate cancer produced sustained increases across multiple vitamin D metabolites over 24 months, accompanied by adaptive shifts in metabolite ratios consistent with regulated catabolic activation, with no clinically meaningful abnormalities in biochemical markers. articles.title: Editorial Expression of Concern: Ligand-independent activation of EphA2 by arachidonic acid induces metastasis-like behaviour in prostate cancer cells.
GSTP1 as a senescence-associated diagnostic candidate in prostate cancer: integrative bioinformatics and functional validation.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a common malignancy of the male genitourinary system with high metastatic potential and poor clinical outcomes, for which effective biomarkers and therapeutic targets remain limited. This study employed a multi-omics approach, integrating transcriptome profiles, age-related gene screening, and machine learning techniques, to analyze four GEO datasets, in order to identify key diagnostic biomarkers for prostate cancer (PCa). Differentially expressed aging-related genes were identified, with enrichment analyses revealing significant involvement in PCa. Using machine learning algorithms, a robust diagnostic model centered on GSTP1 was developed, demonstrating high predictive performance. GSTP1 depletion drove multiple oncogenic phenotypes, including enhanced proliferation, migration, invasion, and the inhibition of cellular aging and DNA damage, suggesting that GSTP1 may promote cellular senescence while restraining malignant progression. Furthermore, its expression correlated with distinct immunocyte profiles, highlighting a role in shaping the PCa immune landscape. Our findings confirm that GSTP1 functions as an aging-associated stress response gene, offering new perspectives on prostate cancer pathogenesis and showing promise for advancing therapeutic strategies that target both aging and immune associations. This study provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging aging biomarkers in precision oncology and highlights GSTP1 as a promising candidate for clinical translation in PCa management.

articles.title: Proteomic Characterization of Prostate Cancer Bone Metastasis Subtypes Defines Progressive Remodeling States of the Bone-Tumor Microenvironment.
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer (PC) bone metastases (PCBM) are a debilitating disease morbidity that primarily affects the axial skeleton. PCBM are predominantly osteosclerotic with mixed osteosclerotic/osteolytic features, including irregular bone deposition, loss of collagen alignment and increased porosity that mimic features of woven bone formed during development and repair. We hypothesize that progression of PCBM is driven by interactions between tumor cells and the bone microenvironment and is associated with changes in the stromal compartment. We performed tandem mass tag mass spectrometry proteomics on lumbar vertebral specimens from 32 cadaveric PCBM specimens and 3 age-matched controls. Unsupervised clustering segregated specimens into three clusters associated with benign, mixed, and osteosclerotic lesion states, characterized by distinct immune-, tumor-, and osteogenic-associated protein signatures. Histological analysis showed tumor infiltration was accompanied by marrow fibrosis and increased collagen III deposition. We identified a marker signature associated with osteosclerotic remodeling and mapped this signature to independent metastatic PC transcriptomic datasets. The proteomics-derived markers reproduced similar molecular groupings at RNA level, and robustly segregated bone PCBMs from soft tissue metastases PC in RNA data. Together, these findings define molecularly distinct states of tumor-driven changes in PCBM that extend beyond histological classification and may inform biomarker development and therapeutic stratification.

articles.title: Androgen receptor signaling in hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms of male predominance and therapeutic opportunities.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is two to four times more common in men than in women. The sex distribution of viral hepatitis, alcohol use and adiposity explains only part of this difference, which points to sex-specific host biology as a further driver. The androgen receptor (AR), a ligand-activated transcription factor expressed in hepatocytes and in most HCC, is a strong candidate: both epidemiologic and experimental data implicate it in the male excess. This review draws that evidence together. Prospective cohorts link higher circulating testosterone and sex hormone-binding globulin to liver cancer risk, although raising SHBG experimentally suppresses rather than promotes hepatocarcinogenesis, a discordance that bears on how those associations should be read, and experimental studies group the underlying biology into several modules: constitutively active AR and its splice variants, kinase-driven phosphorylation of the receptor, downstream effectors of proliferation, invasion and angiogenesis, non-coding RNA circuits, androgen-metabolizing enzymes and the systemic endocrine axis, and the effect of androgen on the tumor immune microenvironment. The weight of each module differs across hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related, hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related, metabolic dysfunction-associated and anabolic steroid-induced disease. Therapeutic work remains largely preclinical and has centered on AR antagonists combined with tyrosine kinase inhibitors or immune checkpoint blockade, on degraders aimed at AR splice variants, on proteolysis-targeting chimeras and nucleic-acid approaches that eliminate ligand-independent receptor states, and on enzyme inhibitors. Two problems still limit translation: AR appears oncogenic in most settings but tumor-suppressive in some, and androgen suppresses antitumor immunity in certain contexts while enhancing it in others. Clarifying when each holds is what will determine whether AR-directed therapy, already established in prostate cancer, can be extended to liver cancer.

articles.title: Lipid Mediators as Therapeutic Targets in Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: Lipid mediators are small molecules, derived from lipid metabolism, that initiate cellular responses. In this review, the major classes of lipid mediators are considered with respect to their effects on prostate cancer cells. These classes are: sphingolipids (sphingosine 1-phosphate and ceramide), glycophospholipids (lysophosphatidic acid; LPA), eicosanoids (prostaglandins, thromboxanes, and leukotrienes), cannabinoids, and free fatty acids. Almost all of these mediators elicit effects by binding to druggable G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) to initiate cell proliferation, stimulate migration, and enhance survival. The exceptions are omega-3 fatty acids and endocannabinoids, which inhibit proliferation. The mediators and their receptors serve as potential targets for (1) enzyme inhibitors that block their synthesis, or (2) GPCR antagonists or agonists. These agents are in various stages of development. Progress in testing their translational potential varies between the mediator classes. Lipid mediators also show potential as diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers. Interesting mechanistic aspects have been identified in the course of studying lipid mediator responses in prostate cancer cells. These include positive cross-talk between LPA receptors and EGF receptors, and negative cross-talk between LPA receptors and free fatty acid (FFA) receptors. Together, these findings suggest new strategies for modulating prostate cancer growth and survival pathways in a therapeutic direction.

articles.title: Early-Apoptotic Responses of Prostate and Melanoma Cancer Cells to 6 MV X-Ray Irradiation in the Presence of Ultrasmall Gold Nanoparticles.
articles.abstract: Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) can modify cellular responses to ionizing radiation. We examined whether 1.9 nm AuNPs alter early apoptosis across a 0-8 Gy dose range in DU145 prostate and MM418-C1 melanoma cells. Cells were incubated with or without 0.5 mM AuNPs for 24 h, irradiated with 6 MV X-rays (0, 2, 4, 6, or 8 Gy), and analysed by Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry 48 h later in three independent experiments. Only adherent cells were collected for analysis; cells detached into the culture supernatant were not included. A two-factor repeated-measures ANOVA tested radiation dose, AuNP exposure, and their interaction. Because sphericity could not be assessed reliably with n = 3, a conservative Geisser-Greenhouse lower-bound correction was also applied to effects involving dose. The uncorrected analysis showed dose × AuNP interactions in DU145 [F(4,8) = 5.26, p = 0.0224, partial η2 = 0.725] and MM418-C1 [F(4,8) = 50.13, p = 1.05 × 10-5, partial η2 = 0.962]. After the conservative correction, the interaction remained significant in MM418-C1 (p = 0.0194) but not in DU145 (p = 0.149). In MM418-C1, AuNP exposure was associated with a higher early-apoptotic fraction at 2 Gy (+5.10 percentage points; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0019) but a lower fraction at 8 Gy (-17.03 percentage points; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0048). No DU145 dose-specific comparison remained significant after Holm correction. The AuNP-associated early-apoptotic response varied with radiation dose and cell line, most clearly in MM418-C1, while the DU145 interaction was less robust under the conservative correction. Given the small number of independent experiments and the 48 h endpoint, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory and not as a direct measure of total cytotoxicity or a specific cell-death mechanism.

articles.title: Concentration-Associated DNA Methylation Remodeling of Oncogenic Signaling Networks Following Moringa oleifera Treatment in Metastatic PC3 Prostate Cancer Cells.
articles.abstract: PC3 prostate cancer (PCa) cells exhibit high metastatic potential, androgen independence, and activation of multiple oncogenic signaling pathways. Although Moringa oleifera has recognized anticancer properties, its effects on DNA methylation in aggressive PCa remain largely unexplored. Here, PC3 cells were treated with Moringa oleifera extract (MO) at 100 or 200 μg/mL and evaluated using functional and molecular analyses alongside genome-wide DNA methylation profiling. Both concentrations reduced AKT phosphorylation and the expression of mesenchymal and invasion-associated markers, whereas increased apoptosis was observed at 200 μg/mL MO. ERK1/2 phosphorylation differed between the two concentrations but was not significantly reduced relative to untreated controls. Methylation profiling revealed concentration-specific pathway-enrichment profiles among genes associated with differentially methylated regions (DMRs). At 100 μg/mL, hypermethylated DMR-associated genes were enriched mainly in small GTPase signaling, focal adhesion, cytoskeletal organization, axon guidance, MAPK, Rap1, and RHO signaling. At 200 μg/mL, enrichment involved cell adhesion, Wnt signaling, RAC1/CDC42 GTPase cycles, and VEGF/VEGFR2-mediated signaling. Hypomethylated DMR-associated genes showed distinct but partly overlapping enrichment profiles. In the direct comparison, DMRs with higher methylation at 100 μg/mL were associated with axon guidance, focal adhesion, actin cytoskeleton regulation, MAPK, and EPH-Ephrin signaling, whereas those with higher methylation at 200 μg/mL were associated mainly with NOTCH and RHOB/RHOC signaling. These findings identify concentration-specific DNA methylation changes in genes belonging to networks relevant to aggressive PCa, accompanied by molecular and cellular responses, without establishing a causal relationship between methylation changes and those responses.
